Sections, stable-first: (1) THE MAP — the richest areas at steering grain; (2) AREA INDEX — every other area, named, one line each; (3) ACTIVE SURFACE — recent + load-bearing witnesses; (4) FOCUS — material loaded for your focus, LAST. The map and index never vary with your focus; your per-call material is at the end.

^-marked entries are compressed stubs carrying child addresses. Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Expand (aswritten_expand with the IRIs you need) before any claim that turns on WHEN or by WHOM something was said, or whether it is still the current framing. Witness-depth sections below already carry full provenance.

Deciding where to go: each mapped area's narration tells you the SPAN of what lives under it; the area index names everything else. Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. But be strict about absence: if neither the map's narrations nor the index's names substantively cover your subject, it is NOT in this perspective — say so rather than expanding a loose thematic match (a word-overlap is not coverage). Decide from the map; expand to ground.

positions.name: OwnedVsRentedIntelligence
positions.frame: what makes intelligence 'owned' rather than merely 'rented', and which layer of it is the asset that persists?
positions.why: src-2 and src-3 together draw one distinction: intelligence held as substrate (a commodity, replaceable, akin to something rented) versus intelligence held as perspective (the asset that is kept). src-4 explicitly names and restates this as 'the individually-owned-intelligence thesis,' confirming the same directional read rather than introducing a separate one — it is positioning language pointing back at the same claim, not a new claim. Pass-2 found no prior position in the perspective for src-4 to bind to (the map and area index carry nothing under this theme), so this is fresh space: a mint, not an attach.

placements.title: Owned intelligence is the asset that persists; substrate is a commodity
placements.theme: The value worth keeping is the owned perspective built atop intelligence, not the underlying substrate, which is a replaceable, rentable commodity.
placements.why: src-2 draws the ownership distinction directly ('owned intelligence is not the same as rented intelligence'); src-3 supplies the mechanism of that distinction (substrate = commodity, perspective = the kept asset); src-4 explicitly names this as a standing thesis ('the individually-owned-intelligence thesis') rather than a one-time claim, which is what makes it leaf-grain under the narrative test — a subject future envelopes can keep feeding, not a fact. Both the existing strata and existing graph structure supplied for this repo are empty, and the position pass confirms this is genuinely new territory (no prior thesis node found at witness depth), so there is nothing to reuse against. No hub or strata category is named by this content itself — it states a directional claim about what constitutes durable value, not an organizational category — so under is left null rather than forcing a strata mint the content doesn't call for.
